origin.description: Fill an array with subarrays. afill uses the dimension names in the value in determining how to fill the LHS, unlike standard array assignment, which ignores dimension names in the value. afill() is a S3 generic, with one method, afill.default, supplied in the abind package.
origin.usage: afill(x, ..., excess.ok = FALSE, local = TRUE) <- value

arguments.text: Arguments that specify indices for x. If length(dim(value)) < length(dim(x)), then exactly length(dim(x)) anonymous arguments must be supplied, with empty ones corresponding to dimensions of x that are supplied in value.

arguments.name: excess.ok
arguments.text: If there are elements of the dimensions of value that are not found in the corresponding dimensions of x, they will be discarded if excess.ok=TRUE.

arguments.name: local
arguments.text: Should the assignment be done on a copy of x, and the result returned (normal behavior). If local=FALSE the assignment will be done directly on the actual argument supplied as x, which can be more space efficient.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: A vector or array, with dimension names that match some dimensions of x.

origin.details: Empty arguments in ... align value dimnames to x. Logical TRUE selects every index on that margin. When value must be replicated to match explicit indices, afill expands value with asub before assignment.
origin.value: The object x is changed. The return value of the assignment expression is the value assigned, as for ordinary subscript replacement.
origin.example:
x <- matrix(0, ncol=3, nrow=4, dimnames=list(letters[1:4], LETTERS[24:26]))
y <- matrix(1:4, ncol=2, nrow=2, dimnames=list(letters[2:3], LETTERS[25:26]))
afill(x) <- y
x

translation.description: Fill an array using value dimnames on dimensions where ... is omitted (None). This follows afill<-.default from abind.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An abind Array or NumPy array to modify in place.

arguments.name: *args
arguments.text: One index per dimension of x when value has fewer dimensions, or exactly len(dim(x)) slots when ranks match. Use None for a missing (empty) argument that takes dimnames from value.

arguments.name: excess_ok
arguments.text: When True, drop value rows or columns whose dimnames are absent from x instead of raising an error.

arguments.name: local
arguments.text: Accepted for API parity with R; assignment always updates the object passed in.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: Vector or array with dimnames (or names for a vector) aligned to the None slots in args.

translation.details: Character and numeric indices follow R rules, including zero indices after nomatch=0 when excess_ok strips value. Replication before assign uses asub when explicit indices repeat a lower-dimensional value.
translation.value: The modified x (the in-place object when x is an Array or ndarray).
translation.example:
from abind.abind import Array
from abind.afill_replacement import afill_replacement
import numpy as np

x = Array(np.zeros((4, 3), order="F"), dimnames=[list("abcd"), list("XYZ")])
y = Array(np.arange(1, 5, dtype=float).reshape((2, 2), order="F"), dimnames=[list("bc"), list("YZ")])
afill_replacement(x, value=y)
print(x)
